changes.title: Explicit self-update
changes.description: ohgo update installs the published release after verifying its SHA-256, and a failed verification restores the previous binary.

changes.title: Complete update lifecycle
changes.description: A successful /update now offers a one-shot What's New acknowledgement on the next interactive launch.

changes.title: Improved TUI update handling
changes.description: The update hint remains informational, installation stays explicit, and the restart requirement is named truthfully.

changes.title: Space jumps to the live edge
changes.description: In the full-screen transcript, `space` returns to the latest line when the composer is idle and the view is scrolled up. A non-empty draft keeps space literal.

changes.title: One-line install
changes.description: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PizenLabs/ohgo/main/install.sh | sh` resolves the latest stable release (or a pinned `OHGO_VERSION`), verifies the tarball against `sha256sums.txt`, smoke-tests the binary, and installs into `$HOME/.local/bin`. A mismatch leaves an existing installation untouched.

changes.title: `/copy` with `-a` and `-c` scopes
changes.description: The default copies the most valuable part of the latest answer without fences; `-a`/`--all` keeps the explanation and every code block, and `-c`/`--context` copies the conversation context. A terminal that cannot accept OSC 52 is reported rather than claiming success.

changes.title: Evidence benchmark suite
changes.description: `go run ./bench/phase9 -suite evidence` measures the five runtime requirement tasks and the authority regression matrix with the real router, security gate, evidence projector, and completion evaluator. It also runs against a live provider with `-live-model`.

changes.title: External-state claims need observation
changes.description: An answer that turns local configuration into a remote fact ("the workflow ran today", "it was pushed") is `NEEDS_REVIEW` unless the run observed the remote surface through a knowledge call, an MCP capability, or a command that talked to a remote.

changes.title: Evidence-aware stop
changes.description: After the first observation turn, a turn that observes the repository without adding a new fact stops informational work from starting another tool round. The decision derives from evidence gain, never from a tool-call count.

changes.title: Repository questions demand evidence
changes.description: Questions about this repository's behaviour ("does this workflow run automatically?") declare a `repository_overview` need that only a content-bearing observation satisfies; a listing or an answer from memory is `NEEDS_REVIEW`.

changes.title: Questions are not execution requests
changes.description: Authority admission no longer escalates an informational question that contains execution or mutation vocabulary, so "I want to ask if this automatically runs" classifies as READ and runs in ASK.

changes.title: "Investigate" routes to FUZZ
changes.description: "Investigate …", "diagnose …", and "troubleshoot …" now classify as INVESTIGATE (FUZZ) instead of falling back to READ.

changes.title: Hosting names are not code symbols
changes.description: Hosting and product names such as "GitHub" are no longer extracted as code symbol targets, so a request that mentions one no longer demands impossible index evidence.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 1
changes.description: the durable task now owns structured, role-independent context (verified facts, hypotheses, evidence references, questions) and isolated ASK/FUZZ/BUILD execution contexts in `progress.json`. Context is assembled deterministically for the active role with existing character and token bounds; it survives restart, session continuation, and task resume, and it never grants authority. Model assertions remain hypotheses until current evidence confirms them, and contradictory evidence is retained without overwriting facts.

changes.title: Task continuity runtime population
changes.description: material tool observations are folded into task evidence references at the turn boundary, successful checks become evidence-backed facts, and ASK/FUZZ/BUILD role contexts carry their own observed progress. A role change on the same objective keeps the task and its contexts instead of detaching it. Semantic hypotheses, questions, reasoning, and strategy remain host writes because the runtime has no trustworthy signal for them.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 2
changes.description: a widening role transition is now a controlled handoff. `workspace.ProposeHandoff` asks for the authority the request needs; the human approves through the existing in-chat transition decision; the existing `SwitchWorkspace` seam performs the only authority move. The task records a bounded handoff (roles, objective, truthfully measured workspace state, and references to the shared facts, hypotheses, questions, evidence, and artifacts) in `progress.json`. Applied handoffs keep one task identity and all role contexts in both directions; rejected, failed, and interrupted handoffs never change the recorded role. A restart reconciles an approved handoff against the authority that was actually restored: a matching target is recorded as applied without a second switch or a resumed turn, a matching source is reported as not applied, and any third role is reported as a recovery discrepancy without rewriting the recorded role. A transition's source is the live authority, so recovered stale task metadata cannot block a valid narrowing, and a checkpoint recovered without `task.md` reconstructs the objective from the contract so its handoff stays valid and writable.

changes.title: Task continuity Phase 3
changes.description: progression, lineage, recovery, and evidence-backed completion. `progress.json` now carries a bounded timeline of meaningful task events (creation, checkpoints, findings, evidence and hypothesis dispositions, handoffs, verification, detach/resume, completion, failure) that references authoritative records instead of copying payloads, plus an evidence proof for COMPLETED tasks. `Task.ObjectiveState` distinguishes `ACTIVE`, `INTERRUPTED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `BLOCKED`, `PROVEN`, `COMPLETED_UNPROVEN`, and `CANCELLED`. Completion is explicit per contract kind: an informational objective needs an answer, an execution objective needs a projected successful execution (an answer alone is refused), and a mutation objective needs an observed change plus a verification that followed it. A proof that is invalidated, superseded, evicted, or materially contradicted downgrades to `COMPLETED_UNPROVEN` without rewriting the lifecycle record. Load reports whether recovery was intact, reconstructed with named missing information, in need of a human decision, or blocked; detached archives carry the same classification and corrupt archive files are reported instead of silently skipped. `/task status`, `/task show`, `/task timeline`, and `/task lineage` expose the same read-only facts through the existing interaction surface.

changes.title: `progress.json` is now schema version 3
changes.description: The bump is a downgrade barrier, not a shape change: a newer binary still reads version 1 and 2 checkpoints, while an older binary refuses version 3 instead of silently rewriting it without the timeline and completion proof it cannot parse. The projection is written before the checkpoint, and the checkpoint write is the commit point.

changes.title: The task timeline elides observation events before lifecycle history and counts dropped events from
changes.description: the retained sequence numbers rather than assuming the first retained event is the creation event. Repeated pause and review boundaries are idempotent, and task-context mutations use the injected clock.

changes.title: A failed completion checkpoint can no longer be published as `COMPLETED`/`PROVEN`: the controller
changes.description: restores the prior task and the TUI refuses to surface an uncommitted completion. The same task stays resumable.

changes.title: A successful command is projected as an observation, so an execution objective can be backed by
changes.description: real execution evidence rather than only by a final answer. The durable boundary also carries a check's reported scope and refuses a verification that does not cover the contract's declared kind and scope.

changes.title: Recovery no longer reports `INTACT` after dropping or repairing a completion proof, archive
changes.description: sanitization reports its repairs, and resuming an archive preserves that classification.

changes.title: A contradiction now downgrades `PROVEN` when it targets a claim the proof depends on, and leaves an
changes.description: unrelated proof intact.

changes.title: Task context selection now uses the fixed budget with relevance ordering instead of recency-only
changes.description: caps: older verified facts survive, the active role's section is reserved, stale evidence cannot displace current evidence, and an overfull section reports how many items it omitted.

changes.title: Task-context repair now deduplicates role contexts across the whole collection, clears dangling
changes.description: supersession pointers, rewrites invalidated confirmations, and refuses to hand back a context that would make every later checkpoint fail validation.

changes.title: A dedup key can no longer silently reuse an earlier record for a different observation, and a fact
changes.description: confirmed from a hypothesis records the confirming role while the hypothesis keeps the proposing role.

changes.title: A quit now cancels an in-flight background update check
changes.description: the observer is bound to the TUI program or plain-REPL lifetime, so leaving ohgo stops the request instead of leaving it running behind a surface that no longer exists.

changes.title: The background check and `/update` now share one update service
changes.description: discovery and installation read and write the same cache, so a hint and an explicit update cannot disagree about which release is current.

changes.title: A cancelled update check is no longer persisted
changes.description: quitting during a check no longer records a failed attempt that suppressed the next eligible check for a TTL.

changes.title: Provider tool-call normalization
changes.description: assistant text that carries a serialized `<invoke>` or `<tool_call>` envelope becomes a canonical tool call before the agent loop or transcript sees it. Every provider stream is normalized, native calls pass through unchanged, and malformed, incomplete, or oversized envelopes stay visible as ordinary text instead of being fabricated or silently dropped.

changes.title: Contextual task rail
changes.description: a responsive right-hand rail shows the active task, its open todos, active integrations, and task insights only while an execution request has open todos. Idle, question-only, and completed or cancelled tasks keep the full-width transcript; a sticky row keeps the task anchored when the rail does not fit, and every section is row-bounded for steady frame cost.

changes.title: `/settings` preferences
changes.description: the new preferences surface toggles the task rail in place and persists it as `taskRail` in `settings.json`, defaulting to enabled. It participates in the shared modal, keyboard, wheel, overlay, composer, and welcome ownership rules.

changes.title: Syntax-highlighted diffs
changes.description: approvals and expanded tool blocks render tinted additions and removals so a mutation can be reviewed without leaving the transcript.

changes.title: Live reasoning and activity
changes.description: throttled Braille spinners mark responding and live-reasoning phases, and one live activity row carries a measured duration plus streaming tool output.

changes.title: Transcript presentation
changes.description: tool runs stay contiguous across streamed text, markdown paragraph breaks survive, reasoning collapses behind a toggle, paths and URLs middle-truncate, and filesystem errors reduce to one-line summaries. Reasoning and tool identity survive session resume, and the recap footer comes from observed evidence and the answer's finding rather than the tool list.

changes.title: Evidence and grounding
changes.description: pruned, truncated, or timed-out scans are incomplete evidence rather than proof of absence; glob output names gitignore-skipped paths, passive search failures are detected, and implementation language is derived from nested manifests the run actually read.

changes.title: Task closure and final answers
changes.description: an answer-only surface withdraws every tool, unproductive turns are bounded, and a failure ledger with provenance attribution keeps the final answer truthful. A blocked task is reported as review rather than success.

changes.title: Provider stream ordering
changes.description: OpenAI and Ollama keep text emitted after a native tool call in its logical position instead of merging it into the trailing block.

changes.title: Closed-surface answers
changes.description: post-answer tool calls are dropped instead of appearing as refusal cards, while policy refusals remain visible in the transcript and session.

changes.title: Informational completion
changes.description: deferred-plan narration ("I will …") no longer completes an informational objective; the run needs an answer.

changes.title: File-count claims
changes.description: exclusive counts are checked against the files the run actually observed.

changes.title: Tool-call leakage
changes.description: serialized calls inside assistant prose no longer leak into visible content or bypass execution; diagnostics name malformed or incomplete envelopes rather than guessing.

changes.title: Session concurrency
changes.description: session startup and sequence allocation are hardened for concurrent writers.

changes.title: Hybrid master-prompt offloading
changes.description: prompts with at least 50 lines or 4000 runes are written to `<project>/.ohgo/scratch/prompt_<session>_<timestamp>.md` and their bytes are injected directly into the model payload. A durable history copy is written first, so Up/Down and Ctrl+P/N still recall the full prompt after scratch is removed. Scratch is cleaned on session close/switch, on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, and by a 24-hour startup sweep.

changes.title: Session protection
changes.description: `t` in the Session Manager toggles a durable `Protected` tag, shown as a star in the status column and as `Protected · yes/no` in the details pane. Tagged sessions are never removed by automatic pruning while explicit deletion still works.

changes.title: Retention controls
changes.description: `/settings` gains a CLEANUP section with auto-prune, keep-recent count, and a manual-clean action. The new `ohgo clean` command performs the same protected-aware pruning from the shell.

changes.title: Deterministic prompt optimization
changes.description: `internal/promptopt` compresses oversized scratch prompts and sanitizes local session titles without a model call or a third-party dependency. Compression removes greetings, politeness, and markdown decoration while preserving fenced code, inline code, paths, and identifiers; local titles drop conversational noise, respect hard word/rune bounds at word boundaries, and never end on a dangling article or preposition.

changes.title: Local-first session titling
changes.description: every session title is derived synchronously from the submitted prompt by `promptopt.SanitizeTitle` before any provider request. The background ASK-model titler, its timeout and backfill workers, and the "generating title…" placeholder are removed. Legacy untitled sessions are labeled locally when the Session Manager opens, so titles appear instantly with zero token cost.
